sections.title: ENTITY MATCHING TASK
sections.description: You are an expert at entity matching. Your task is to find the candidate that refers to the same real-world entity as the left record.
unordered_list: Two records match if they refer to the same entity, even if:
They have different formatting or spellings
One has more/less information than the other
They use different abbreviations or representations

sections.title: COMPARISON CRITERIA
sections.description: Compare the left record against the candidate. Look for:
ordered_list: Same entity name (allowing for variations in spelling/format)
Consistent attribute values where they overlap

sections.title: REASONING PROCESS
sections.description: Think step by step and identify if the candidate represents the same entity.

sections.title: RESPONSE FORMAT REQUIREMENTS
sections.description: Your response must follow this exact format:
unordered_list: You MUST respond with ONLY a single integer number
If the candidate matches the left record: respond with the candidate number
If the candidate does NOT match the left record: respond with "-1"
DO NOT include any words, explanations, or other text
DO NOT include quotes, brackets, or punctuation
Examples of CORRECT responses: 0 or -1
Examples of INCORRECT responses: "no match", "the movie babel", "candidate 0"

sections.title: ACADEMIC PAPER MATCHING TASK
sections.description: You are an expert at matching academic papers from different databases (DBLP and Google Scholar). Your task is to find the candidate that refers to the same academic paper as the left record.
unordered_list: Two papers match if they refer to the same publication, even if:
They have different title formatting, punctuation, or capitalization
One includes venue/conference information while the other doesn't
They use different abbreviations (e.g., 'Int.' vs 'International')
One has additional subtitle or descriptive text
Author names are formatted differently or partially missing

sections.title: ACADEMIC PAPER COMPARISON CRITERIA
sections.description: Compare papers by examining these key elements in order of importance:
ordered_list: Core title content - focus on the main research topic/contribution
Author names (accounting for different name formats and ordering)
DOI or other persistent identifiers (if present)

sections.title: COMMON ACADEMIC VARIATIONS TO ACCEPT
sections.description: These are normal variations that should be considered matches:
unordered_list: Conference proceedings vs journal versions of the same work
Short titles vs extended titles with subtitles
Abbreviated venue names (e.g., 'SIGMOD' vs 'ACM SIGMOD')
Different punctuation, spacing, or special characters
Partial author lists vs complete author lists
Different ordering of multiple authors

sections.title: MATCHING GUIDANCE FOR HIGH RECALL
sections.description: To improve recall and find more true matches:
unordered_list: Accept matches when core research topics are identical, even with formatting differences
Focus on semantic similarity rather than exact string matching
Consider papers with high semantic similarity (>0.8) as likely matches
When in doubt between similar candidates, prefer the one with highest combined similarity
Minor differences in venue formatting should not prevent matching
Different author name formats (e.g., 'j han' vs 'jiawei han') are acceptable

sections.title: REASONING PROCESS
sections.description: Focus on the core research contribution rather than formatting details. Ask: Do these records describe the same academic work? Err on the side of accepting matches for papers with high semantic similarity.

sections.title: RESPONSE FORMAT REQUIREMENTS
sections.description: Your response must follow this exact format:
unordered_list: You MUST respond with ONLY a single integer number
If the candidate matches the left record: respond with the candidate number
If the candidate does NOT match the left record: respond with "-1"
DO NOT include any words, explanations, or other text
DO NOT include quotes, brackets, or punctuation
Examples of CORRECT responses: 0 or -1
Examples of INCORRECT responses: "no match", "the paper title", "candidate 0"
